data.name: Mashari
data.long_meaning: One who shows the way or guides others towards a goal. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'mashar' which means 'path' or 'way'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are spiritual guides and mentors, inspiring others to find their way towards enlightenment and inner peace.

in_arabic.name: ماشاري
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من م ش ر، يعني منشأ أو منبع
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من م ش ر، والذي يعني منشأ أو منبع. وقد وردت هذه الجذور في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنبياء: 'وَمَشَارِ كَثِيرَةً' (الأنبياء: 25). وقد استخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة العربية الإسلامية كاسم للذكور، ويعبر عن الأصول والمنابع النبيلة.

in_urdu.name: ماشاری
in_urdu.meaning: ماشاری نام کا مطلب ہے مشرقی یا سورج کی طرف سے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ماشاری ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے مشرقی یا سورج کی طرف سے۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، خاص طور پر م ش ر سے، جو قرآن کریم میں بھی ذکر کیا گیا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کی روایات میں، یہ نام اہل تشیع کے لیے خاصی اہمیت رکھتا ہے، کیونکہ مشرق یا مشاری کا تعلق امام علی ابن موسیٰ الرضا کے مشہور لقب 'مشرق الانوار' سے ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मशारी
in_hindi.meaning: मशारी नाम का अर्थ है पूर्व दिशा या सूर्योदय
in_hindi.long_meaning: मशारी एक पुरुष नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है पूर्व दिशा या सूर्योदय। यह नाम अरबी मूल से निकला है, विशेष रूप से म ش ر से, जो कुरआन में भी उल्लेखित है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम विशेष रूप से शियाओं के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि पूर्व या मशारी का संबंध इमाम अली इब्न मूसा रज़ा के प्रसिद्ध उपाधि 'मशरिक अल-अनवार' से है।

in_pashto.name: ماشاري
in_pashto.meaning: ماشاري د لمر پورې اړه لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: ماشاري د پسټو ژبې يو نوم دی، چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوی دی. دغه نوم د م ش ر څخه مشتق دی، چي په عربي کې د لمر پورې اړه لري. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، دا نوم د سولې، رڼا او لارښوونې د نښې په توګه کارول کېږي. د اسلامي نړۍ په تاريخي متنونو کې د مشرق يا ماشاري په اړه خاصه يادونه شوې ده.

in_english.name: Mashari
in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic root 'mashr', meaning eastern or sunrise
in_english.long_meaning: Mashari is a masculine given name originating from Arabic roots. It is derived from 'mashr' (م ش ر), which signifies eastern or sunrise. This name has been used in Islamic tradition, particularly among Shia Muslims, associating it with the concept of 'mashriq al-anwar' (eastern light), a title attributed to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida. The name symbolizes enlightenment, nobility, and spiritual guidance. Across Muslim cultures, Mashari is valued for its historical and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mashari holds immense cultural significance as it signifies the person who provides guidance and defines the path for others. It highlights the importance of leadership and mentorship in Islamic culture. In Islamic tradition, prophets and scholars have been referred to as 'Hudah' or guides, who have illuminated the path towards truth, wisdom, and enlightenment for their communities. This name honors individuals who have followed the path of knowledge and wisdom themselves and then strive to help their fellow beings navigate their own journeys.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual plane, the name Mashari holds great significance because it signifies being on the 'straight path' towards Allah, as mentioned repeatedly in the Quran. Islamic teachings emphasize the importance of remaining on the path of righteousness and truth, following the guidance of Allah and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Therefore, the name Mashari not only symbolizes guidance and leadership towards worldly goals but is also deeply connected to spiritual growth, reminding the person bearing the name to remain steadfast on their spiritual journey towards Allah.

historical_references.reference: Mashari ibn Al-Ash'ath Al-Farghani was a Persian Muslim mathematician and astronomer. He made significant contributions to the field of trigonometry and is considered the founder of algebraic trigonometry. He lived during the Abbasid Caliphate, in the late 8th and early 9th centuries.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliphate, significant contributions to trigonometry

historical_references.reference: Mashari Al-Qadimi was an early Islamic scholar and poet from Basra. He was a contemporary of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida and is best known for his collection of hadith, 'Kitab al-Asma' wa Sifat Rasul Allah' (The Book of Names and Descriptions of the Messenger of Allah). This book is considered one of the most reliable sources of the Prophet's names, attributes, and actions. He lived during the early Islamic period, around the 9th century.
historical_references.time_period: Early Islamic period, around the 9th century
historical_references.context: Contemporary of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, reliable source of Prophet's names and actions
